The instant Appeal has been filed by the Appellants challenging the compensation granted on account of the death of the deceased driver in an accident by the Commissioner for Employees Divisional Manager vs Lagnajit Lenka & Ors on 24 December, 2025

1
Compensation in E.C. case No. 179-D/2019.
I. FACTUAL MATRIX OF THE CASE:

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
Location: ORISSA HIGH COURT, CUTTACK (i) That the claimants-respondents filed an application bearing E. case No. - 179-D/2019 before the Commissioner for Employees Compensation claiming compensation on account of the death of the deceased driver, Manoranjan Lenka in an accident which occurred on 19.8.2019.

(ii) While the deceased was doing the work as a driver under the Opp. Party No.-1- Respondent No.-5 in his Truck bearing registration No.- OR-21-9777 and proceeding towards Keonjhar met with an accident with another truck and as a result, the deceased sustained injuries and died at the hospital on the same day while under treatment.

(iii) That the aforesaid case was adjudicated by the learned Employees Compensation-cum-Joint Commissioner on 15.9.2021, directing the appellant to pay compensation of Rs.7,97,600/- with an interest @ 12% from 19.8.2019 to 15.9.2021 i.e., Rs.1,99,028/- as such the total compensation is Rs.
9,96,628/-.

II. ISSUES:
(i) Whether the deceased was an employee within the meaning of E.C. Act, 1923?
(ii) Whether the accident and accidental injuries sustained by the deceased employee resulting his death arose out of and in course of his employment under the OP No.1?
(iii) Whether the applicants are entitled to get compensation as claimed or any part thereof?
Location: ORISSA HIGH COURT, CUTTACK (iv) Whether the opposite parties are liable to pay any compensation to the applicants, if so, by whom it is payable?
III. SUBMISSIONS ON BEHALF OF THE APPELLANT:
3. Learned counsel for the Appellant earnestly made the following submissions in support of his contentions:
(i) The appellant-insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation amount on the ground that the deceased driver had no valid/effective D.L. at the relevant Divisional Manager vs Lagnajit Lenka & Ors on 24 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16883627/
2 time of accident which expired on 26.11.2018.

(ii) The learned Commissioner awarded the compensation ignoring this fact and relied on a decision reported in TAC 2006(2)599 of the High of Himachal Pradesh which is not applicable in the present case and saddled the appellant with the compensation amount.

(iii) It is a settled position of law, in view of Judgment passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No.7220 and 7221 of 2011 that owner of the vehicle under which the deceased driver was employed having no valid D.L. is liable to bear the responsibility and consequent liability, and the Insurance Company could not have been held liable to indemnity for the owner, to satisfy the claim.
(iv) When an employer employs a driver, it is his duty to check that the driver is duly licensed to drive the vehicle.

Section 5 of the Motor Vehicle Act provides that no owner or person in-charge of Location: ORISSA HIGH COURT, CUTTACK a Motor vehicle shall cause or permit any person to drive the vehicle if he does not fulfil the requirements of Section 3 and 4 of the Motor Vehicle Act.

(v) In compliance with the Section 30 of EC Act, the Insurance Company deposited the entire awarded amount of Rs. 9,96,628/-
before the learned J.L.C, Cuttack on 13.12.2021.
Accordingly, the deposited compensation amount with accrued interest thereon may be refunded to the appellant for just decision of this case.

(vi) In light of these findings, the reference was answered accordingly, and the matter was remitted to the Hon'ble Single Judge for disposal in accordance with law.
IV. SUBMISSIONS ON BEHALF OF THE RESPONDENTS:
4. On the contrary, the Learned Counsel for the Respondents made the following submissions:
(i) The Respondents-claimants filed an application before the learned Commissioner claiming compensation on account of the death of the deceased driver, Manoranjan Lenka in an accident which occurred on 19.8.2019.
( ii) The Opp. Parry No.-l, the employer admitted the employment of the deceased as a driver and the death arising out of and in course of his employment.
He also claimed indemnification of its liability, if any, against Opp. Party No.-2, insurer in view of the valid insurance coverage.
On the other hand, the O.P. No.-2 denied the entire claim.
Location: ORISSA HIGH COURT, CUTTACK Divisional Manager vs Lagnajit Lenka & Ors on 24 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16883627/

3 (iii) The P.W. -1 was examined and cross examined and exhibited the documents under Ext.- 1 & 11 and filed a copy of the D.L. of the deceased driver to prove the death of the deceased out of and in course of his employment under O.P. No.-1.

(iv) The O.P. No.-2, in order to prove his stand that he is not liable to indemnify the owner stated that there had been a violation of the policy conditions as the driver had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the transport vehicle.
(v) He filed the certified copy of the D.L. of the deceased driver under Ext.- A, to prove that the deceased driver had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the transport vehicle.
Hence the insurer is not liable to pay the compensation.
(vi) The O.P. No.-2 filed the present appeal U/S.-30 of the W.C. Act., mentioning the Substantial question of Law.

So far as the violation of the policy condition is concerned, the provision of the section 149 of the M.V. Act, 1988 is not applicable for the W.C. Act., hence the insurer is not allowed to take the benefit available under that provision in the W.C. Act.
(vii) The insurer did not prove a deliberate and wilful violation of the policy conditions by the owner as merely filling one certified copy of the D.L. does not prove it.
Hence, the insurer is liable to indemnify the owner as there was a valid policy to cover the risk of the driver.
Location: ORISSA HIGH COURT, CUTTACK

(viii) It is submitted that the decision of the Apex court reported in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v Mastam1, M/S. National Insurance Co. Ltd. v Panibudi Chulia2 and National Insurance Co. Ltd. v Soubhagini Nayak3 support this claim.

V. FINDINGS OF THE COMMISSIONER:
5.
The learned Employees Compensation-cum-Joint Commissioner for Workmen's Compensation heard the parties, perused the documents on record, and upon the basis of the pleadings decided upon the matter.

(i) The Commissioner in issues 1 & 2, upon examining the written statement of OP No. - 1, and oral evidence of PW1 supported by certified copy of Ghatagaon PS Case No. 98/2019 and other documents, held that the death arose out of and in the course of employment.
(ii) The Commissioner, on examination of the evidence available on record held that the deceased had a valid driving licence and accordingly saddled the liability on the appellant.

(iii) In absence of any contrary evidence from the side of the OP No. 2 and basing on the own admission of the applicant, the Commissioner held the age of the deceased as 34 years old at the time of accident.

Divisional Manager vs Lagnajit Lenka & Ors on 24 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16883627/
4 2005 AIR SCW 6305 2006 (l) OLR (FB) 715 FAO. No.- 141 of 2023

sentences.text: Location: ORISSA HIGH COURT, CUTTACK

(iv) Regarding wages, the applicants have stated in their claim application as well as in the evidence of PW No, 1 that the deceased was getting Rs. 10,000/- PM from OP No. - 1 towards v/ages at the time of accident.

(v) In TAC 2006(2) 599 in which the Court vouched that, even if the deceased driver not have a valid driving license at the relevant time of accident, the Insurance Company is held liable to pay compensation under the EC Act.

(vi) Accordingly, the Commissioner, by its reasoned judgment in E. case No. - 179-D/2019, allowed the claim application and stated the respondent was liable to pay compensation to the appellant on account of death of the deceased and rejected the insurer's plea of violation of policy conditions.
VI. THIS COURTS'S JUDGMENT AND ANALYSIS 6.

The present appeal under Section 30 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 has been preferred by the appellant-Insurance Company assailing the judgment and award passed by the learned Employees' Compensation-cum-Joint Commissioner for Workmen's Compensation in E.C.
Case No.179-D/2019, whereby compensation amounting to 9,96,628/- was awarded in favour of the claimants on account of the death of the deceased driver, and the liability was fastened upon the insurer.

7. The appeal has been admitted on the substantial question of law as to whether the Insurance Company can be held liable to indemnify the Location: ORISSA HIGH COURT, CUTTACK employer when the deceased driver did not possess a valid and effective driving licence at the time of the accident.

Since the appeal is confined to a question of law, this Court does not sit as a court of first appeal on facts, but is required to examine whether the findings of the Commissioner suffer from perversity or misapplication of settled legal principles.
8. The foundational facts are not in dispute.
The deceased, Manoranjan Lenka, was admittedly employed as a driver under Opposite Party No.1, the owner of the vehicle.
His death occurred on 19.08.2019 in an accident arising out of and in the course of his employment.
The employer accepted the relationship of employer and employee and also admitted that the death occurred during the course of employment.
The only contest before the Commissioner, and now before this Court, pertains to the liability of the insurer in view of the alleged absence of a valid driving licence.

9. The appellant-insurer specifically pleaded and adduced documentary evidence to show that the driving licence of the deceased driver had expired on 26.11.2018 and had not been renewed as on the date of the accident.
The certified copy of the driving licence was marked as Ext.-A.
The accident having occurred on 19.08.2019, it is evident on the face of the record that the deceased did not possess a valid and effective driving licence on the relevant date.

5 10.

sentences.text: The learned Commissioner, however, proceeded to hold that the deceased had a valid driving licence and fastened liability on the Location: ORISSA HIGH COURT, CUTTACK insurer.
This finding, in the considered opinion of this Court, is ex facie unsustainable, as it runs contrary to the documentary evidence on record.

Once the licence stood expired long prior to the date of accident,
the conclusion that the deceased had a valid driving licence is clearly perverse and unsupported by evidence.
11. The legal consequence of absence of a valid driving licence now falls for consideration.

It is a settled principle of law that when an employer engages a driver, a statutory duty is cast upon him under Section 5 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 to ensure that the person employed to drive the vehicle holds a valid and effective driving licence.
Permitting a person without a valid licence to drive the vehicle constitutes a clear breach of statutory duty as well as a violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

12. The learned Commissioner relied upon a decision reported in TAC 2006 (2) 599 of the Himachal Pradesh High Court to hold that even in the absence of a valid driving licence, the insurer remains liable under the Employees' Compensation Act.
This Court finds that such reliance is misplaced.

Subsequent authoritative pronouncements of the Hon'ble Supreme Court have clarified the law that where the employer has committed a fundamental breach of policy conditions by employing a driver without a valid licence, the insurer cannot be compelled to indemnify the employer.
Location: ORISSA HIGH COURT, CUTTACK 13.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in Beli Ram vs Rajinder Kumar4 has categorically held that when the driver does not possess a valid and effective driving licence, the liability cannot be fastened upon the insurer and the responsibility must fall upon the owner-employer who permitted such driving in violation of law.
The ratio laid down therein squarely applies to the facts of the present case.

14. The contention advanced on behalf of the claimants that Section 149 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 is not applicable to proceedings under the Employees' Compensation Act is correct to the limited extent that the statutory defences available under Section 149 cannot be bodily imported.
However, this does not mean that the insurer can be fastened with liability even where there is a fundamental breach of the insurance contract.

The liability of the insurer under the Employees'
Compensation Act flows from the contract of insurance, and once a breach going to the root of the contract is established, the insurer cannot be compelled to indemnify the employer.
15. The further argument that the insurer failed to prove wilful or deliberate violation of policy conditions by the employer is also without merit.
When the driving licence itself had expired months prior to the accident, the employer is deemed to have constructive knowledge of such fact.
Employment of a driver without verifying the validity of his licence constitutes negligence per se and amounts to breach of statutory duty under Section 5 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Civil Appeal Nos. 7220 and 7221 of 2011

Insofar as the reliance placed by the claimants on decisions such as National Insurance Co. Ltd.
v. Mastan, National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Panibudi Chulia and National Insurance Co. Ltd. v.
Soubhagini Nayak is concerned, those decisions were rendered on their own factual matrix where either the licence was valid or the breach was not established.

sentences.text: The said authorities do not lay down an absolute proposition that the insurer is liable in all cases irrespective of absence of a valid driving licence.

17. In the present case, the insurer has discharged its burden by producing cogent documentary evidence establishing that the deceased driver did not possess a valid and effective driving licence on the date of the accident.
The learned Commissioner failed to appreciate this evidence in its proper perspective and erroneously saddled the liability upon the insurer.
18. This Court, therefore, holds that the finding of the learned Commissioner fastening liability on the appellant-Insurance Company suffers from a substantial error of law.
The compensation awarded to the claimants is not interfered with; however, the liability to satisfy the award must rest upon the employer, Opposite Party No.1, and not upon the insurer.

19. Since the appellant-Insurance Company has already deposited the entire awarded amount along with accrued interest in compliance with Section 30 of the Employees' Compensation Act, it is entitled to refund Location: ORISSA HIGH COURT, CUTTACK of the said amount, subject to adjustment, if any, in accordance with law.

VI. CONCLUSION:
20.

In view of the foregoing discussion and reasons recorded hereinabove, this Court is of the considered opinion that the impugned judgment and award passed by the learned Employees'
Compensation-cum-Joint Commissioner for Workmen's Compensation in E.C. Case No. 179- D/2019 cannot be sustained in law to the extent it fastens liability upon the appellant-Insurance Company.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.

21. The judgment and award passed by the learned Employees' Compensation-cum-Joint Commissioner for Workmen's Compensation in E.C. Case No. 179-D/2019 is hereby modified to the extent that the liability to satisfy the awarded compensation shall rest upon Opposite Party No.1-the employer/owner of the vehicle, and not upon the appellant-Insurance Company.

22. The compensation amount awarded in favour of the claimants is maintained; however, the appellant-Insurance Company is held not liable to indemnify the employer in view of the established absence of a valid and effective driving licence held by the deceased driver at the time of the accident.

23. Inasmuch as the appellant-Insurance Company has already deposited the entire awarded amount of 9,96,628/- along with accrued interest before the learned Commissioner in compliance with Section 30 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, the learned Commissioner is Location:

ORISSA HIGH COURT, CUTTACK directed to refund the said amount with accrued interest, if any,

24.
